commands.review_summary:
The PR adds an `archivedOnly` `sessions.delete` parameter, makes `sessions.delete` dynamically authorize write-scoped archived deletes, keeps the kill HTTP endpoint admin-only, and updates Android to delete only archived rows with that flag.

PR surface: Source +76, Tests +89, Other +6. Total +171 across 11 files.

Reproducibility: yes. source-reproducible: current schemas reject unknown delete params and Android/gateway protocol constants remain v4, so a new Android client can connect to an older v4 gateway and then fail the archived delete request. I did not run a live Android/gateway pairing.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Manual review is required because the remaining blocker is a protocol/security-boundary choice, not a safe mechanical repair.

target.title: feat(gateway): archive-gated session deletes give Android delete parity
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Android session Delete control shipped in #100814 silently fails: it calls `sessions.delete`, which requires `operator.admin`, and Android's bounded operator session (`nativeClientOperatorScopes`) never requests admin. This is the same scope gap that #100964 fixed for `sessions.patch`, left open then as a product decision (documented in #100712's closeout) because deletion is a different risk class.

## Why This Change Was Made

Archive-then-delete, expressed as an explicit API opt-in:

- `sessions.delete` gains an additive `archivedOnly: boolean` param (protocol schema + regenerated Swift models). With `archivedOnly: true`, the dispatcher grants `operator.write` (params-aware dynamic scope, same mechanism as `sessions.patch` in #100964) and the handler requires the target to already be archived — destructive intent stays a deliberate two-step action (archive from the list, then delete from the archived view).
- Without the flag, nothing changes: deletes require `operator.admin`. Internal fallback/synthetic dispatch (default `[operator.write]` client), subagent cleanup of unarchived child sessions, and CLI least-privilege minting keep their existing admin contracts — the `server-plugins.test.ts` fallback-delete contract test passes unchanged. An earlier draft gated on caller scopes inside the handler; structured review correctly flagged that this loosened internal synthetic dispatch, so the gate moved to an explicit param.
- The session-kill HTTP endpoint previously borrowed the `sessions.delete` static method scope; it now pins `operator.admin` explicitly, since it terminates live runs rather than deleting archived records.
- Android sends `archivedOnly: true` and its session menu offers **Delete only on archived rows** (where the gateway now authorizes it); active rows archive first, so no dead buttons. The archived-row Delete flow already existed from #100814. iOS/web connect with admin and keep unrestricted deletes.
- Existing delete guards are untouched: main-session block, lifecycle CAS, plugin-runtime ownership mismatch checks, webchat mutation rejection.

## User Impact

Android users can delete sessions (archive first, then delete from the Archived view). No behavior change for admin clients, internal callers, or run-kill authorization.

## Evidence

- Unit tests (`method-scopes.test.ts`): `sessions.delete` least-privilege stays `[operator.admin]` without the flag; `archivedOnly: true` resolves/authorizes at write scope; read scope and non-boolean flag values are denied.
- WS tests (`server.sessions.store-rpc.test.ts`): a write-scoped client deleting without the flag gets `missing scope: operator.admin`; with the flag on an active session gets "Archive it first"; with the flag on an archived session succeeds and empties the archived list.
- Hosted Testbox (Blacksmith): `method-scopes`, `server.sessions.store-rpc`, `server.sessions.delete-lifecycle`, `session-kill-http` (52), `server-plugins` (fallback-delete contract), and `subagent-spawn` suites — 603 tests pass; `tsgo:core` + `tsgo:core:test` green; `pnpm android:test` green; `pnpm protocol:check` deterministic; oxfmt clean.
- Codex structured review (fast tier): the first cycle's P1 (synthetic fallback loosening) drove the archivedOnly rework; final commit reviewed clean.

Refs #100712 (follow-up explicitly deferred there and in #100964).
